touches.text: Tool: a complete primitive. Has users, not an owner. Calls no other Cairn component (stdlib and base only) and owns no state of its own. Lives in cairn/tools/ (17). Its data for a holder lives under that holder: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/.

Mail goes to the bus, and from the bus to the shims. If the bus has to start a shim to deliver, it may hold that mail in a transient tree (4.3.2) until the shim is up. That is mail waiting on a wake; 5.5.3.4.1 is mail nobody picked up.
The shims, each connected to the bus, pick up the messages and route them to their device in whatever manner is appropriate.
Processes all messages from the bus for its device.

base shim: the base class for every shim, customized for the device it interfaces with, internal or external. Carries the panes every device has (2.3.8), the scheduler (5.9), and the [all] verbs (2.4.11.2).

open_questions.text: Proofs in tester, codemother and librarian (8 imports, measured 2026-11-11) stand up a scratch bus in their own process by importing the cairn device's bus machine (BusDevice.scratch, BusShim), so they can drive their shim against stub devices. Does the cairn device get a fourth exception at 2.3.7.1, a published scratch-bus tool for proofs? Or do those teeth ride the live bus through bus_client and lose their stubs? CC's read: publish it. A proof needs a bus it controls, and db_domain's published client already carries scratch() the same way.
